title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-06-02
content:
Attendance: Aisha, Marco, Priya, Daniel, Sofia (remote)

TL;DR:
- Observed a p95 latency regression (~8-12%) and ~6% throughput drop for chat workloads after merging kernel-switch PR (#987) into canary. Regression most pronounced at seq_len=512 and batch sizes 4-8 on A100-40GB nodes.
- CI nightly perf job reproduced regression locally; canary traffic shows same pattern but lower magnitude due to sampling.
- Immediate plan: rollback kernel-switch on canary, collect full perf traces, run focused microbench matrix, and add coverage to CI.

Notes / discussion:
1) Repro summary:
   - Baseline (master before PR987): p95=210ms, p50=42ms, tokens/sec=1200 (seq=512, batch=8)
   - Canary (post PR987): p95=235ms, p50=44ms, tokens/sec=1128 (seq=512, batch=8)
   - Degradation larger at higher seq lengths (256->512 amplifies p95 delta).
   - Observed small increase in CPU-side scheduling spikes during decode.

2) Tests run:
   - nightly/perf-chat-large (CI): reproduced on x3 runs, artifacts in linked_artifacts.
   - local microbench: bench/run_microbench --model redwood/ggml-13b-q4 --seq 512 --batch 8 --kernels dynamic+quant. Scripts and raw outputs attached to run id above.
   - latency profiling: capture via perf+traces; sample traces show longer time in MatMul kernel invocation path and increased memcpy latency on host->device for certain quant kernels.

3) Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
   - Kernel selection fallback in PR987 sometimes picks a slower quantized matmul path for specific tensor shapes (most likely).
   - Dynamic batching scheduler changes slightly increased head-of-line blocking for batches with variable length (observed in traces).
   - KV-cache eviction policy interaction: extra memcpy when cache pages misaligned due to kernel layout changes.

4) Immediate actions (owners / ETA):
   - Roll back PR987 on canary and re-run A/B perf tests (owner: Marco Liu, ETA: 2026-06-03 morning).
   - Run expanded microbench matrix across seq_len={128,256,512,1024} and batch={1,2,4,8} on A100 and H100 (owner: Daniel Kim, ETA: 2026-06-04).
   - Collect per-request traces + nvprof for worst-case runs and upload artifacts (owner: Priya Natarajan, ETA: 2026-06-04).
   - Add deterministic kernel-selection test to CI that validates slower alternative isn't chosen for shapes seen in chat workloads (owner: Sofia Martinez, ETA: 2026-06-10).
   - File an action JIRA with prioritized severity and attach repro steps + artifacts (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-06-02 end of day).

5) Longer-term mitigations:
   - Improve kernel-selection heuristics to prefer throughput-optimized kernels for common chat shapes; add cost model parameters.
   - Expand perf regression alerts to include p95 deltas per seq_len in addition to global p95.
   - Add synthetic load generator to simulate mixed-length batches to catch HOL blocking regressions earlier.

6) Observations from logs/traces:
   - Slightly higher memcpy times on host->device for quant kernels (~1.2-1.5x).
   - Increased tail-latency correlation with GPU occupancy dips (suggests suboptimal kernel launch sizing).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we want an immediate revert for PR987 on master, or keep revert only on canary until root cause confirmed? (Decision deadline: 2026-06-03 EOD)
- How aggressive should CI be in running expanded microbench matrix (time/cost tradeoff)?

Meeting decisions to capture now:
- Revert on canary only for now (Marco to execute).
- Run full microbench across prod-supported hardware (Daniel).
- Add CI test to block kernel-selection regressions (Sofia).

Action items (recap):
- Marco: rollback PR987 on canary + rerun perf baseline (ETA 6/3).
- Daniel: run matrix on A100/H100 and post results (ETA 6/4).
- Priya: collect nvprof/perf traces and upload to artifacts (ETA 6/4).
- Sofia: implement CI kernel-selection test (ETA 6/10).
- Aisha: file JIRA PERF-423 with repro and label P1 (done).

Next sync: perf-benchmarking weekly sync on 2026-06-09 10:00 PT. Add results to the perf tracker and update the linked confluence page with final findings.

Notes to self: keep a copy of microbench script (bench/run_microbench) with --trace flag for future runs; if we see >5% p95 delta on seq=256 or 512 mark urgent.

Attachments: raw bench logs uploaded to run id benchmark-artifacts://runs/2026-06-02-kernelexp, perftools traces in same run.
